headline: Project HOPE housing program: council votes 8-1 to create a resolve accepting MaineHousing money.
summary: The one-year pilot would add a housing navigator at each of three shelters, Preble Street, Bangor Area Homeless Shelter, and Community Care, plus one at the city. MaineHousing would pay 70% of the cost, and the 30% match would come from shelter funds and city staff time. Staff set a goal of serving 90 people and placing at least 45 into stable housing, and the resolve will go to council.
decisions: Approved creating a resolve to accept and appropriate MaineHousing money for Project HOPE, 8 yes and 1 no.
Approved entering executive session on personnel matters under 1 MRSA 405 6A, with a roll call of yes votes.
discussion: Project HOPE: Members asked about the program goal, past city funding to the shelter, and landlord support. Staff said the one-year pilot would aim to serve 90 people and place at least 45 in stable housing.

CSX railroad property: Members asked why trash built up and whether the area could be fenced or blocked off. The city manager said CSX planned to finish cleanup along the tracks by Thanksgiving, and staff would evaluate fencing with the railroad.

Roux Institute AI tool: The city manager said Bangor Public Health was asked to sit on the institute's responsible AI advisory board. Any future grant to bring the tool to Bangor would come before council, and the advisory role has no funding now.

Public comment timing: The chair raised trying public comment at the start of meetings instead of the end. One member favored trying it, another had no preference, and the chair said he may test it at a future meeting.
